fields.explanation: Keep the original n=16,d=8 trace with all eight draws at r1. Its simple neighborhood is {r1}, so degree is one. A generic constant-draw theorem confirms the same defect for every positive number of draws, covering arbitrarily large fourth-power sizes without replacing the original witness. The finite image of the actual sampling function is exactly the simple neighborhood. The headline proves the fourth-power parameter relation, singleton image, degree one and negation of the universal degree-eight claim; the generic theorem establishes image cardinality one for all d>0.
fields.flaw: The stated random construction, which chooses d=n^{3/4} neighbors with replacement and then treats multiple edges as a single edge, guarantees every left vertex has simple degree exactly d.
fields.problem:
Problem
Apply the probabilistic method to prove the existence of a bipartite graph satisfying the
following conditions for all sufficiently large integers n.
Let the graph consist of vertex
partitions L and R such that: (i) Both partitions have cardinality |L| = |R| = n; (ii) The
degree of every vertex in L is exactly n3/4, while the degree of every vertex in R is bounded
above by 3n3/4; (iii) For any subset S ⊆L with cardinality |S| = n3/4, the neighborhood of
S in R has size at least n −n3/4.
1

fields.witness:
n=16,d=8, all draws hit r1 → deg 1

Take any fourth-power n with d=n^{3/4}>=2; concretely n=16, d=8. In the construction, let one left vertex l1 choose r1 in all 8 draws. This is a valid sampling trace. After multiple edges are collapsed to a single edge, l1 has simple neighborhood {r1}, so its degree is 1, not 8. Thus exact left degree is not guaranteed by the construction.
